liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (5 reviews): Reviewer likes that Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain came in an unusual spot in the show; Second set was slow with newer tunes until a very well played Scarlet-Fire, with a favorite jam coming out of Scarlet [16][17][19][21][23]
- **Loose Lucy** (3 reviews): Loose Lucy was still new to the repertoire and sounded strong in the first set; Reviewer especially liked the Loose Lucy [17][22][23]
- **Cold Rain & Snow** (2 reviews): Opening with Cold Rain & Snow in the unbearable heat struck the listener as a funny, unexpected choice; Opening with Cold Rain & Snow on such a hot day is taken as nice sarcasm [17][26]
- **Just A Little Light** (1 review): Brent's wailing on Just A Little Light is called the highlight of his career, shortly before his death [19]
- **Loser** (1 review): Loser is singled out as a nice performance [20]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): Reviewer considers this one of the best versions of The Wheel [22]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd90-07-04d1t01**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd90-07-04d1t02**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd90-07-04d1t03**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd90-07-04d1t04**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd90-07-04d1t05**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd90-07-04d1t06**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd90-07-04d1t07**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd90-07-04d1t08**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]

## The recordings

- **gd90-07-04.sbd.miller.26351.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 165 min; rated 3.87/5 by 30 [1]
- **gd1990-07-04.154442.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 169 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [6]. Said about its sound: A bad cable affected the right channel in set 2; the left channel was pasted over those spots; For U.S. Blues the soundboard feed to the ultra box was off, leaving only ambient mics [6]
- **gd1990-07-04.153738.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 20 songs; 169 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [7]. Said about its sound: A bad cable hurt the right channel in set 2; left channel was copied over the affected passages; The soundboard feed was switched off for U.S. Blues, so only ambient microphones are heard [7]
- **gd1990-07-04.sbd.miller.tetzeli.fix-26351.81523.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 170 min; rated 3.5/5 by 12 [8]

## Around the show

- About 105 degrees at showtime, with the stage facing west; Jerry wore shorts and repeatedly wiped his guitar neck [18]
- First set was short; Weir said the band would return once it cooled off, and mud covered the grounds [18]
- Afterward a fireworks war broke out in the parking lot, with adults behaving like young kids [18]
- Temperature was 106 degrees at showtime, and heat exhaustion sent many fans to the medics [19]
- Last time this listener saw Brent before his death; the heat was brutal, with garden hoses and mud slides [21]
- Parking lot asphalt seemed to be melting in the heat [21]
- Parking lot fireworks afterward resembled a bottle rocket and roman candle war, frightening the listener [22]
- Reviewer finds the show tepid and says other summer 1990 shows are better choices [20]
- Reviewer found more energy here than at the Dead shows seen later [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd90-07-04.sbd.miller.26351.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> Dat> Cassette Master [1]. Also: Cassette master transferred via ART DIO at 24bit/96k, Sound Forge 7, CD, EAC, then SHN by Charlie Miller [1]
- **gd1990-07-04.154442.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  October 4, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-X90) [6]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; multiple masters were combined to make the show complete [6]
- **gd1990-07-04.153738.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  October 4, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-X90) [7]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; multiple masters were used to complete the show [7]
- **gd1990-07-04.sbd.miller.tetzeli.fix-26351.81523.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: Patched fix of shnid 26351 [8]. Also: Drums section from 1:25 to 6:57 was patched in from Ladner's audience recording, shnid 8573; Based on Charlie Miller's soundboard seed; SHN files converted to FLAC and SBEs cleaned up with shntool [8]

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Sandstone Amphitheatre - July 4, 1990](https://www.dead.net/show/july-4-1990) [30]

claims.text: Reviewer likes that Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain came in an unusual spot in the show
Opening with Cold Rain & Snow in the unbearable heat struck the listener as a funny, unexpected choice
Loose Lucy was still new to the repertoire and sounded strong in the first set
Second set was slow with newer tunes until a very well played Scarlet-Fire, with a favorite jam coming out of Scarlet
About 105 degrees at showtime, with the stage facing west; Jerry wore shorts and repeatedly wiped his guitar neck
First set was short; Weir said the band would return once it cooled off, and mud covered the grounds
Afterward a fireworks war broke out in the parking lot, with adults behaving like young kids
Temperature was 106 degrees at showtime, and heat exhaustion sent many fans to the medics
Brent's wailing on Just A Little Light is called the highlight of his career, shortly before his death
Reviewer judged the Scarlet-Fire the standout of the night, outdoing everything else
Loser is singled out as a nice performance
Reviewer finds the show tepid and says other summer 1990 shows are better choices
Last time this listener saw Brent before his death; the heat was brutal, with garden hoses and mud slides
Brent was on fire during Scarlet; the performance felt earth-shaking, and the sky changed color
Parking lot asphalt seemed to be melting in the heat
Reviewer considers this one of the best versions of The Wheel
Reviewer especially liked the Loose Lucy
Parking lot fireworks afterward resembled a bottle rocket and roman candle war, frightening the listener
Reviewer says Loose Lucy was unbeatable
Scarlet-Fire was top notch, danceable boogie
Reviewer found more energy here than at the Dead shows seen later
Opening with Cold Rain & Snow on such a hot day is taken as nice sarcasm
Soundboard went to DAT, then to a cassette master
Cassette master transferred via ART DIO at 24bit/96k, Sound Forge 7, CD, EAC, then SHN by Charlie Miller
Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; multiple masters were combined to make the show complete
A bad cable affected the right channel in set 2; the left channel was pasted over those spots
For U.S. Blues the soundboard feed to the ultra box was off, leaving only ambient mics
Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; multiple masters were used to complete the show
A bad cable hurt the right channel in set 2; left channel was copied over the affected passages
The soundboard feed was switched off for U.S. Blues, so only ambient microphones are heard
Drums section from 1:25 to 6:57 was patched in from Ladner's audience recording, shnid 8573
Based on Charlie Miller's soundboard seed; SHN files converted to FLAC and SBEs cleaned up with shntool
